PullRequest.Title: Agent Host: add experiment-capable settings for two runtime cache flags
PullRequest.Body:
Add two off-by-default, experiment-capable settings that the agent host sends to the Copilot SDK as runtime feature flags:

- chat.copilot.fusion.sentHistoryAdoption.enabled sends HYDRAFUSION_SENT_HISTORY_ADOPTION: after a Copilot Fusion turn commits, the session keeps the request history the committed phase sent, so the next turn extends the cached prompt instead of rewriting it.
- chat.copilot.contextBudgetToolEstimate.enabled sends CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOOL_ESTIMATE: context measurements taken before a request count deferred tools the way the next request sends them, rather than every tool schema in full.

The runtime's own experiment assignments do not reach VS Code sessions, so these flags can only be turned on from VS Code through a setting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and live configuration forwarding for the two experiment-capable settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution computes four scalar root values and dispatches changed values asynchronously; it does not await host persistence, customization refresh, or automation refresh before the workbench can continue. A session launched before forwarding completes may observe prior configuration, but that is correctness/config timing rather than a performance block.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch RootConfigChanged from the workbench to the local agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold upgrade or changed experiment assignment: four actions for the two value/default-control pairs; a direct change to one setting can produce two actions. Warm startup: zero actions because structural equality suppresses unchanged values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These four keys did not exist, so they generated no root-config IPC actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and not awaited by contribution startup; it does not block workbench progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the full persisted root config, mkdir the parent, write a temporary file, and rename it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized write transaction per accepted RootConfigChanged action: at most four for initial hydration of these keys, then zero on warm starts unless a value changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No persistence transactions existed for these absent keys; other forwarded settings already use the same per-key persistence path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued on _rootConfigWrite and not awaited by the originating workbench dispatch, so it is off the interactive critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute agent descriptors and queue customization publication for registered sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Triggered once per accepted action, so four cold-start passes; per-session Copilot customization reads share settled discovery, and RootMcpDiscovery performs its filesystem scan only on the first cold refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These keys caused no passes, though every existing root-config update already used this broad invalidation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued/asynchronous and guarded by equality/cached discovery; no changed request waits for all session refreshes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant four new keys, with secondary in-memory/mostly cached work scaling with registered sessions. Effective filesystem scan cardinality is one per distinct cold workspace root because RootMcpDiscovery is shared and initialized after its first scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four workbench pushes may start concurrently; host config writes are serialized by _rootConfigWrite, customization publications are serialized per session, and root MCP discovery is serialized/shared per root.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Missing persisted keys cause cold dispatch and writes. Persisted equal values suppress all four actions on warm startup. Customization and MCP discovery retain settled/shared state; only the first cold root discovery scans .mcp.json.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the four-action/four-write cold mechanism and its suppression on warm starts, based on the forwarder equality guard and serialized persistence implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of restored sessions varies, but expensive filesystem persistence is fixed at four cold transactions and is off the critical path. No evidence shows user-visible startup latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable: the added boundary work is finite, asynchronous, warm-cache suppressed, and follows the existing forwarding architecture; no concrete user-visible regression is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot SDK session with either runtime cache experiment enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session configuration is assembled before the existing SDK createSession/resumeSession call. The diff adds two root-config reads and at most two boolean properties to that existing payload; it adds no awaited operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send session config through the existing SDK create/resume boundary to the Copilot runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one existing create or resume operation per launched session; the diff only extends featureFlags by zero to two booleans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single SDK create/resume operation occurred without HYDRAFUSION_SENT_HISTORY_ADOPTION or CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOOL_ESTIMATE.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing create/resume remains on the launch critical path, but its call count and scheduling are unchanged; the payload growth is constant.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Copilot runtime model-request path reached after session launch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model requests whose prompt-history/cache behavior may be selected by the new runtime flags
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing model request per turn/phase; this diff does not add a request or increase concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same requests were sent with runtime-default history adoption and context estimation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model requests are critical to response latency, but the supplied repository contains no runtime implementation showing added work; the documented behavior is cache-prefix reuse and avoiding unnecessary compaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of created/resumed sessions and subsequent turns. Boundary cardinality remains one launch per session and one existing model request per turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged from the launcher: independent setup work is already combined with Promise.all, and the feature-flag reads add no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Flags are off by default. When experiment-enabled, sent-history adoption is intended to extend the prior cached prompt and tool estimation is intended to avoid unnecessary compaction; no repository evidence establishes cache invalidation or retention growth.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that this diff changes only constant-size configuration and not launch/model boundary cardinality; low confidence about undocumented SDK internals, so no adverse behavior is inferred.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The downstream SDK implementation is outside the supplied repository, so exact token/cache savings are unknown; importantly, there is also no code evidence of a regression mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable: no added boundary call, eager work, concurrency burst, or proven cache-lifecycle regression is introduced by the diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Process a routed Fusion turn and attribute the two setting experiments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On session.fusion_resolved, the host synchronously checks default-control/assignment state and calls the existing telemetry helper. Telemetry submission is not awaited before Fusion progress processing continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two events per telemetry service/process across all Fusion turns because experimentTrigger.ts deduplicates treatment names in a WeakMap-backed Set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two setting treatments emitted no trigger events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The helper runs in event handling but does not await network I/O; after the first routed turn, calls reduce to Set lookups.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fusion resolutions can occur once per routed turn, but external telemetry cardinality is capped at two per process; subsequent turns perform two constant-time map/set checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fusion events are handled in the existing session event stream. No Promise fan-out or concurrent network burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first eligible route populates the telemetry deduplication Set. All warm routes are negative lookups followed by early return; pending treatment names are bounded to the two settings while assignment context is absent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the helper's explicit per-telemetry-service deduplication and the bounded pending Set.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry implementation buffering details are not shown, but the strict two-event cap and non-awaited call remove realistic scaling risk.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable: bounded telemetry and constant-time warm-route checks do not create a concrete throughput or latency regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct the Copilot CLI subprocess environment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Environment construction remains a single linear scan performed before the existing subprocess launch. The diff enlarges constant lookup sets and removes inherited experiment flags; it performs no new I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare environment for the existing Copilot CLI subprocess spawn
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing environment build/spawn per client start; no subprocess is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same environment scan and subprocess launch occurred without filtering the newly named flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Environment filtering is on startup, but remains O(number of environment variables) with constant-time Set membership and only a few additional constants.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of inherited environment variables and Copilot client starts; asymptotic work and boundary count are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous environment filtering followed by the existing client-start lifecycle; no new parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Added Set entries only affect membership results for specific keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete function body.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the constant Set-size increase is negligible and does not change scaling.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not reportable: no meaningful CPU, allocation, I/O, or subprocess regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced settings forwarding, persistence/invalidation fan-out, SDK session launch, Fusion telemetry, and subprocess environment construction. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
